newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Wheat, maize futures mixed, barley down in Hungary.
newsitem.headline: Wheat, maize futures mixed, barley down in Hungary.

text.p: Falling feed barley futures were the main movers on the Budapest Commodity Exchange (BCE) grains section on Friday, with most other grains ending mixed, traders said.
"Feed barley usually follows price drops in other grains with a significant phase delay," Sandor Ifju of OTP Forex said.
Feed barley prices dropped by 100 to 300 forints, except for the September maturity which remained unchanged.
Maize futures prices ended mixed, going up for May and July by 70 and 160 forints per tonne respectively, and dropping for November and December by 300 and 100 forints respectively.
Milling wheat futures rose slightly for most new (1997) crop maturities but dropped for March to 25,000 forints, down 100, and for May to 23,330 forints, down 320.
Friday's total turnover was 638 contracts or 256.04 million forints, with 282 contracts.
Most grain futures have fallen since Tuesday and traders said speculation and rumour would remain the determining market factors until hard news in mid-March.
"Most old (1996) crop prices have been on a downward slope since Tuesday," Ifju said.
Turnover remained below average throughout the week except for the May maturity of most grains as traders were closing speculative March positions and opening new ones for May.
There are 1,038 open contracts for March milling wheat and 1,980 for May, and 2,740 open March contracts for maize versus 4,152 for May.
Ifju said physical deliveries were behind the majority of the March contracts, but late speculation could cause sudden price movements by the end of the month.
"Some players could wait until the very last day," he said.
Lot size is 20,000 kgs for all contracts.
